acceptance.criteria: Every unsandboxed Windows command requires AIW approval, including risk strategy version 0.
acceptance.evidence: COMMAND calls flow through GuardBroker.operate and _requires_approval. On win32, needs_approval is unconditionally true after policy validation; the non-Windows version-0 bypass is explicitly excluded. Approved replay validates the frozen command and APPROVED state.

acceptance.criteria: Windows startup checks ProcessSpawnParams before advertising guarded-command-v1.
acceptance.evidence: Windows calls protocol_capability(process_spawn=True), which requires ProcessSpawnParams and all fields used by process/spawn. The capability is added only after that check succeeds. Linux/WSL still requires CommandExecParams.

acceptance.criteria: Missing Codex App Server is reported as an execution dependency, not a sandbox dependency.
acceptance.evidence: ManagedWorkerProvisioner maps CODEX_EXECUTABLE_UNAVAILABLE to wording that Windows command execution needs Codex App Server and retains executable-path and external Worker guidance.

acceptance.criteria: Timeout, output cap, cancellation, Job Object cleanup, and Linux/WSL behavior remain intact.
acceptance.evidence: Windows request carries timeoutMs/outputBytesCap; Worker enforces a local deadline and cumulative output cap, and checks outputDrainTimedOut. Cancellation interrupts session receive; finally closes a kill-on-close Job Object and waits for zero active processes. Linux/WSL remains on sandboxed command/exec with cgroup limits and populated=0 cleanup.
